caveats: The market is hard to beat. Over the last 3 years the rule's tickets won 126 of 369 (+5% a ticket, -10% to +20%); the market-only control's won 110 of 346 (-3%). An interval that spans zero is no evidence of an edge.
Measured to 2026-08-08, the last day all three sports' leg tables cover (UFC 2026-08-08, NFL 2026-11-08, soccer 2026-11-08); the UFC walk-forward needs a runner refit to go further.

Prices: UFC at each card's closing (or, where only that exists, opening) line, NFL at the closing moneyline, soccer at the pre-match average posted on Friday or Tuesday afternoon. A ticket built earlier in the day gets different prices; NFL closing lines know the day's news.

Payouts: these files' margins are lower than a single sportsbook's live prices (NFL closing 2.8% a game, the median here, against 4.0% on the 45 games the NFL app logged live), so a live ticket pays a little less than the record assumes.
Soccer here is the top five leagues only, which play no matches on international-break weekends and in June-July; on those days a ticket comes from UFC and NFL alone, or there is none.
UFC days are the event date; a card held outside the Americas can fall on another ET date.
The likeliest ticket in 3-5x is mostly favourites, and every leg is the same model's opinion; the legs are different events, so their outcomes are close to independent.

caveats: The market is hard to beat, and a draw cannot create an edge: every 3-5x ticket pays the bookmaker's margin on every leg. This ticket is for variety and a bigger payout, never the better bet. At the live salt it won 397 of 1487 (-2% a ticket, -10% to +7%); an interval that spans zero is no evidence of an edge.

Expected before any result was seen (sameday.py): by the prices it lands about 1 time in 4 (a market chance of about 0.25 at about 3.8x), the likeliest about 2 in 7 at about 3.1x, price-implied about -8% a ticket, and somewhat worse than its prices imply. The prices on file give it a market chance of 0.244 at 3.83x, price-implied -8.5%.

Prior exposure: the rule's own results were not seen before it was fixed, but underdog results over the same years had been - the UFC profiles' risker and risk-lover tickets and the NFL and soccer edge-betting checks. Its record is not an out-of-sample test of underdogs.

Bookmakers load more margin on underdogs (about 5% on a dog leg against 3% on a favourite, as written before the results), so a dog ticket pays the heavier margin once on its dog and a lighter one on each favourite that fills it; the fill adds payout, not safety or value.

The market chances here take the margin off in proportion, which reads a dog's chance generously. Taking it equally off each side (Shin's reading for two sides), the 3,316 UFC dogs priced 2.00-4.00 average a chance of 0.363 against 0.368 and return -5.6% at their price against -4.0%; the 2,157 NFL dogs 0.364 against 0.368, -4.3% against -3.0%. Soccer's split is missing: these files keep the two teams' prices, not the draw's.

NFL underdogs are chosen and priced at the closing moneyline (197 of the live salt's 1487 dogs): the close knows the day's news, and whether a dog is priced 2.00-4.00 is decided at it; live, both are decided at the consensus price when the ticket is built.
UFC cards of 2025 are priced at their opening lines (no closing line is on file for them): 24 of the live salt's UFC dogs that year, 36 of its 266 UFC dogs in all priced at an opening line.

The 5th-95th percentile across the 1,000 simulation salts (-15.6% to -4.3% a ticket over all days) is how much the draw alone moves the record over the same games; it is not a confidence interval. The interval over days is (-9.9% to +7.0% at the live salt).

Live, a UFC leg is priced from the card the UFC app carries (the best price across books, or a median of books where the card has one); this history prices each fight at one line per card. A live UFC dog's price, and whether it falls in 2.00-4.00, can differ from what this record assumes.
Same days and events as the likeliest ticket: on the 1132 days both exist, the two cannot both win on 102 (the dog is the other side of one of the likeliest ticket's legs).
